test_readout.youtube: The YouTube push worked: its whole range is a gain. It came in above the model's forecast but inside its range, so it agrees with the model.
test_readout.search: Pulling non-brand search back showed no clear drop. That side was a guardrail with low odds of seeing the drop the model expected, so it does not show search does nothing. It only rules out a big hidden loss.
test_readout.rules: Neither guardrail tripped, so the rollout followed the refit model, as written down before the test.

rollout.what: From June, the refit model's plan in the rollout markets at the same total budget: more Meta, YouTube, connected TV, LinkedIn and affiliates, less display retargeting and less non-brand search. The holdout markets, the ones in neither group of the spring test, stayed on the old plan so the rollout could be measured against them.
rollout.readout: The rollout worked: its whole measured range is a gain.
rollout.model_view: The model's own view of the rollout is shown beside the holdout as a cross-check. It uses no outcomes and decides nothing, and the model is likely to under-credit paid media.
rollout.budget: The rollout moved money between channels inside the same budget; it added no new spend except the brand search that follows extra searches.
rollout.totals: The year's totals hold everything that moved in 2026: the spring test, the rollout, sales headcount, the market and the season. They describe the year; they do not measure the rollout. The holdout does.

next: Keep the rollout plan into the new year, and refit the model on the full year with the holdout result added.
Keep a smaller holdout running, because a holdout this size can only see a large effect.
Test non-brand search again with a bigger and longer pullback. It is still the biggest and least measured channel.
Hold Meta flat in a few markets through a busy season, so the model can tell Meta from the season.
